extracted.intended_audience: registered patent agents/attorneys, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, legal counsel and adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order under 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b) imposing an interim suspension of a patent practitioner based on proof of a serious crime, outlining notice/service requirements, referral to a hearing officer, publication and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension (37 C.F.R. §11.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension of practice before the USPTO may be ordered pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b) where proof shows the Respondent committed a serious crime (the Notice/Order requested interim suspension predicated upon proof of conviction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order relied on a certified copy of a state Order of Conviction showing conviction of two counts of use of a minor in filming sexually explicit conduct (West Virginia Code §61-8C-2) as the basis for interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical violations under 37 C.F.R. §10.23 (basis for discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim suspension was ordered for violation of the ethical standards set out in 37 C.F.R. §§10.23(a), 10.23(b)(3), 10.23(b)(6), and 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of these disciplinary ethics provisions can constitute grounds for disciplinary action including interim suspension; the Order identifies those specific regulatory sections as the rules violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice mailing and address requirement (37 C.F.R. §11.11 / §11.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed to the most recent address provided by Respondent to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.11 (mailed first-class certified mail, return receipt requested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order documents the certified mail receipt number and USPS tracking information showing delivery. Proper mailing to the last known address is an essential procedural step for the Notice and Order under §11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond and 40-day response period (37 C.F.R. §11.25(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order directed Respondent to file, within forty days, a response containing information sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must present facts creating a genuine issue of material fact within the 40-day window to avoid interim suspension or to contest the factual predicate for the interim order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (no genuine issue of material fact)
rubrics_metrics.description: More than forty days passed without a response from Respondent; accordingly, it was determined there is no genuine issue of material fact pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b) and interim suspension and referral of the Complaint was appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely respond to the Notice and Order permits the OED/Director to conclude there is no genuine issue and proceed with interim suspension and referral for formal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceeding (37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is referred, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(5), to a hearing officer for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order identifies the hearing officer (Chief Administrative Law Judge) and provides mailing/hand-delivery addresses for submission of the Respondent's answer to the Complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file written answer to Complaint (37 C.F.R. §11.36) within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to file a written answer to the Complaint in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.36 within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order with the identified hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides specific mail and hand-delivery addresses (Office of the Administrative Law Judges, EPA) for submitting the answer and emphasizes the 30-day deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to serve copy of answer on OED Director within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must serve a copy of his answer to the Complaint on the OED Director by mail to Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, United States Patent and Trademark Office, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, Virginia within thirty (30) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely service on the OED Director is a separate procedural obligation in addition to filing with the hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Interim Suspension (37 C.F.R. §11.59(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59(a), shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette detailing the interim suspension, including the practitioner's name, registration number, nature of the conviction, and sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order includes the precise Notice of Interim Suspension text (name, registration number, conviction details, sentence) and directs posting of disciplinary decisions at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to notify employees, agencies, courts, and state authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of this Final Order to: (1) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (2) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (3) appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order mandates cross-notification to relevant internal and external stakeholders as part of implementing the suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations during suspension (37 C.F.R. §11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.58 sets forth practitioner obligations during suspension (e.g., notice to clients, handling of files. The Order requires adherence to those regulatory duties while suspended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures (37 C.F.R. §11.25(e) and §11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.25(e) should Respondent seek reinstatement; the pending disciplinary proceeding may result in an initial decision imposing discipline which would require compliance with 37 C.F.R. §11.60 to be reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order identifies the regulatory provisions governing how a suspended practitioner may seek and obtain reinstatement following an initial decision or interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between inactive status and exclusion on consent (37 C.F.R. §11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: As a result of an earlier letter (Oct 16, 2009), Respondent was placed in an inactive status; he was not excluded on consent pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order clarifies practitioner status labels (inactive vs. excluded on consent) and references the governing regulation for exclusions on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certified conviction documents as evidentiary basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim suspension request was predicated upon proof that Respondent committed a serious crime, namely a certified copy of a March 23, 2011 Order of Conviction and Order of Commitment showing conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified court orders of conviction may serve as sufficient documentary proof to support disciplinary actions such as interim suspension under the USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for disciplinary action (35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.25, 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§11.25 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the federal statutory and regulatory provisions empowering the USPTO Director and OED to impose interim suspensions and to publish disciplinary notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions regarding practitioners are posted at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room electronically located at: http://des.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs where the public can access disciplinary decisions, indicating a transparency/publication practice for these orders.
